title: automate-ocsp-stapling-and-hsm-failover-for-private-installer
author: Isabel Chen
description: Automates OCSP stapling configuration and HSM failover handling for private deployments. Motivation: customers operating in VPC/on-prem environments require continuous TLS validity checks and zero-downtime key failover when an HSM node is unreachable. This PR introduces: 1) a Helm chart hook that deploys an ocsp-stapler sidecar (configurable) and ties stapling refresh cadence to Vault/PKI TTLs; 2) Terraform modules to provision a lightweight health-proxy and DNS failover records for HSM endpoints (optional for air-gapped installs); 3) an operator-style pre-upgrade check that validates active OCSP stapling and HSM primary/secondary sync before allowing helm upgrades; 4) backup flow for private key escrow using sealed-secrets + metadata-encrypted snapshots uploaded to customer-configured object store; 5) a safe rollback path that replays the previous stapled responses and promotes the prior HSM key if a rollout fails. The description below includes implementation notes, compatibility, and rollout guidance. Implementation notes: The ocsp-stapler is a small Go container that queries the configured CA for OCSP responses and stapled responses into the ingress TLS termination (nginx/contour). It uses the existing KMS plugin interface to sign internal health tokens and reads keys from mounted HSM PKCS#11 volumes when present. If HSM is unavailable, the stapler switches to a cached signed-staple mode and triggers a failover reconciliation to the health-proxy. Helm: new templates under charts/private-installer/templates/ocsp-stapler.yaml, a post-install hook to bootstrap the stapler state, and values.yaml toggles for enabling stapling and configuring TTL multipliers. Terraform: modules/hsm_failover adds optional aws_route53 or internal-dns entries (module toggles) and a health-proxy EC2/container definition with a lightweight leader-election lock stored in the existing Vault cluster. Upgrade safety: pre-upgrade hook implemented as a helm test (templates/preupgrade-check.yaml) that runs a small validation job verifying stapling freshness, HSM reachable primary/secondary status, and sealed-secret snapshot presence. Rollback: hooks preserve last-known stapled responses in an annotation on the TLS secret; rollback job restores those annotations and forces ingress reload. Secrets handling: sealed-secrets workflow encrypts escrowed private-key snapshots and stores manifest pointers in Vault for audit. For air-gapped installs we support local object-store backends (minio) and an offline sealed-secrets reconcile mode. Security: HSM interaction strictly follows PKCS#11 interface, and we added additional timeout and retry policies to avoid accidental key promotion on transient network issues. Compatibility: works on both OpenShift and upstream k8s distributions; ingress integrations covered: nginx-ingress, contour, and envoy via SDS. Backwards compatibility: enabling the feature is opt-in via values; when disabled, no changes to existing cert flows. Rollout guidance: enable in canary namespaces, monitor stapling_hit_rate and stapling_age metrics (new metrics added), and validate key promotion alarms in SLO console before scale. See release_notes for upgrade steps.

release_notes: Opt-in: OCSP stapling + HSM failover automation. Add charts/private-installer.values to toggle. Adds Terraform module for optional DNS failover and health-proxy. Adds sealed-secrets-based private-key escrow snapshots and rollback safety. See docs/private-installer/upgrade-notes-ocsp.md for step-by-step upgrade guidance.
notes_for_ops: 1) Enable feature in canary namespace first. 2) Ensure Vault retain policy for escrow snapshots is configured. 3) If using HSM, verify PKCS#11 plugin path is correct in values.yaml. 4) Watch stapling_age and stapling_hit_rate; alert if stapling_age > CA_TTL*0.9. 5) For air-gapped installs use the internal-dns toggle and local S3 endpoint.
